findings.F1: The Wednesday (UTC) move reverses the move from Saturday's close to Tuesday's close, and the reversal is graded. On Tuesday bars, the Spearman correlation between the 3-day vol-scaled return and Wednesday's excess return is -0.137 (p 6e-10, 2033 cases). This is the strongest of the 7 weekday tests, which otherwise range from -0.08 to +0.03. With the cases of one day taken together, -z3 × Wednesday excess has a t of 2.11 over 346 days.

findings.F3: The tested idea's grading holds in the bars. Saturday's excess return in the forecast's direction rises with |forecast|, from -0.20 % (t -0.88) in the lowest quintile to +1.01 % (t 4.79) and +0.87 % (t 3.69) in the top two. All 6 coins are positive (+0.36 % to +0.53 %).
findings.F4: Part of the book's Saturday gain is plain Saturday drift. The Friday-close-to-Saturday excess return is +0.30 % unconditionally (t 2.07 by day, 414 days). In the upper half of the yearly range, Saturdays after a midweek fall, where the book is flat, also rise (+0.33 %, t 1.89).

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's return from Saturday's close to Tuesday's close (UTC), measured in its usual daily moves, the more the coin moves the other way over Wednesday. A weekend-to-Tuesday rise is followed by a Wednesday fall, and a fall by a Wednesday rise, each larger the larger the 3-day move.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean against a coin's weekend-to-Tuesday move over Wednesday, in proportion to the size of that move, and would refuse Wednesday trades in the direction of that move.
ideas.name: Wednesday reverses weekend move

ideas.idea: While a coin's last 20 days have been volatile relative to its own history, the larger its one-day fall in usual daily moves, the more it rises over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy a coin after a sharp down day in a high-volatility stretch, scaled to the size of the fall, and would refuse to short it into the next day.
ideas.name: High-volatility down-day bounce
